BAIL APPLICATION No. - 9633 of 2024 Applicant :- Arun Kumar Opposite Party :- State Of Up And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Awadhesh Bahadur Sinha,Sadrul Islam Jafri,Sr. Advocate Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

Shri Suchit Tandon, learned AGA for the State contends that the police authorities in compliance of the directions issued by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 46998 of 2020 (Junaid Vs State of U.P. and another) reported at 2021 (6) ADJ 511 and with a view to implement the provisions of POCSO Act, 2012 read with POCSO Rules, 2020, have served the bail application upon the victim/legal guardian as well as upon the CWC.
By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
244 of 2023 at Police Station-Kokhraj District-Kaushambi under Sections 376(3), 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 20.06.2023.

sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 03.11.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Sadrul Islam Jafri, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Suchit Tandon, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 14 years in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2.The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no lawful basis for the age related entry of the victim in the school records.
The school records disclosing her age as 15 years are unreliable.
(iii) The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has stated that she is 14 years of age.
(iv) Medico-legal examination (not the age determination test) records that the victim is 16 years of age.
(v) The medical report drawn up to determine the age of the victim opines that she is 15-17 years of age.
Two submissions are made in regard to the aforesaid medical report.
Firstly, the range of error in determining the age is about two years and the same should be read in favour of the applicant at this stage.
Secondly, the relevant scientific parameters as per latest medical protocol which would establish the majority of the victim has been excluded from consideration in the medical report.
The medical report is flawed.
In fact the victim is a major.
2. The victim and the applicant were residing in the same neighbourhood.
They grew fond of each other over the years and became intimate.
3. The victim and the applicant were found together in a compromising position.
4. The F.I.R. was lodged after the said relationship got exposed and to deflect attention from the conduct of the victim.

sentences.text: 5. False and aggravated allegations have been made by the victim against the applicant in her statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. at the behest of her parents only to to deflect attention from her own conduct and to save the failing prosecution case.
7. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim did not raise an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
Her conduct shows that she was a consenting party.
8. Major inconsistencies in the F.I.R. statements of the victim under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. discredit the prosecution case.
9. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
10. The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated with the police investigations and had joined the trial proceedings.
11. The applicant did not influence the witnesses or tamper with the evidence.
13. The applicant never adopted any dilatory tactics or impeded the process of the trial.
14. The trial has moved at an inordinately slow pace.
The applicant is not responsible for the delay in the trial.
15. Status report sent by the learned trial court records that as per the chargesheet the prosecution proposes to examine 8 witnesses to bring home the charges.
Two prosecution witness including the victim have already been examined.
There is no possibility of the applicant influencing the witnesses or tampering with the evidence.
16. Inordinate delay in concluding trial had has led to virtually an indefinite imprisonment of the applicant without there being any credible evidence to implicate him in the offence.
Right of the applicant to speedy trial has been violated.
17. The applicant has to gather various defence evidences to be tendered before the trial court to prove to get himself exonerated.

18. Continued incarceration of the applicant will disable him from framing an effective defence strategy, gathering evidence in his support thereof and tendering the same before the learned trial court to absolve himself of the charges.

19. This Court in Prabhat Gangwar v. State of U.P. (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.2586 of 2023) while considering the grant of enlarging an accused on bail for preparing his defence and gathering evidence to tender the same before the learned trial court for establishing his innocence held:

sentences.text: "Nature and gravity of the offence is certainly liable to be considered by the court while considering grant of bail.
The Court has also to factor the likelihood of whether the accused committed the offence while deciding a bail application.

The court also has to determine in the facts of the case whether the accused needs to be set at liberty to frame his defence and gather evidence to refute the prosecution case and establish his innocence.
The bail court has to examine whether continued incarceration would disable the accused from tendering an effective defence of his case.
This is a demand of processual fairness in criminal jurisprudence.
Setting an accused at liberty at large on this ground cannot be applied mechanically in all cases.
The issue has to be considered in the facts and circumstances of each case while doing so.

All relevant facts including the evidences in the record, the conduct of the accused during the investigation as well as trial have to be adverted to before a decision is made in this regard."
20.
The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
21. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
Considering the aforesaid parameters in light of the above facts of this case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled for bail.

In wake of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case,
the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant - Arun Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
